fichas.title: Skylights and dome rooflights
fichas.summary: Dome rooflights and skylights can provide daylight and ventilation, clear smoke, and provide roof access. North-facing domes help avoid sunshine and glare; a high curb can reduce glare from low sun. For ventilation, orient rooflights toward prevailing winds, with the inlet aperture smaller than the outlet. A fan in the curb can provide forced ventilation. Smoke exhaust systems require attention to aerodynamic extraction and wind orientation.

fichas.summary: The illustrated continuous rooflight arrangements include multiple-barrel, barrel, double-pitched, and single-pitched forms. The diagrams give widths for several configurations. Skylight systems are described as providing diffused room lighting free from glare.

fichas.title: Monitor and saw-tooth rooflights
fichas.summary: The illustrated rooflight types include monitor rooflights with inclined or vertical panes and 60° and 90° saw-tooth north lights. North-facing saw-tooth skylights with spun glass fibre inlays are described as providing climatically beneficial workshop lighting. The diagrams show widths and rooflight-unit dimensions.
